description: Window functions with PARTITION BY: the result must be computed PER PARTITION, not across all rows. Every assertion here is deliberately partition-sensitive - it gives a different answer if PARTITION BY is ignored, which is the previous behaviour that treated the whole result as one partition. The decisive one is that id 3 (Sales, 80) is the third-highest salary OVERALL but the TOP of the Sales partition, so its ROW_NUMBER is 1 and not 3. Then: ROW_NUMBER = 1 once per partition gives two rows where a single partition would give one; the top two per partition gives four where a single partition would give two; RANK restarts the same way; PARTITION BY two columns whose pairs are all unique makes each row its own partition so all five qualify; and no PARTITION BY at all leaves one partition, where the top two are two rows. Converted 1:1 from query/WindowPartitionByTest (now retired); the Java scanned for a given id with a cursor loop and asserted row counts, so the converted tests pin the whole ordered row set.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, salary INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn FROM emp ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, salary INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn FROM emp QUALIFY rn = 1 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, salary INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn FROM emp QUALIFY rn <= 2 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, salary INTEGER)
SELECT id, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rk FROM emp QUALIFY rk = 1 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, salary INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dept, salary ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM emp QUALIFY rn = 1 ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE emp (id INTEGER, dept VARCHAR, salary INTEGER)
SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn FROM emp QUALIFY rn <= 2 ORDER BY id
